Issued at 1254 PM CDT Fri Sep 4 2026

Tonight - Monday: Persistent Shower/Storm Chances, Trending Slightly
Cooler

A quasi-stationary boundary remains draped across the Upper 
Mississippi River Valley through the rest of the afternoon and 
into tonight, mainly south of I-90. While forcing along the 
boundary is fairly weak, some showers and storms have been able
to develop with additional development possible (10-30%) into 
this evening. Plenty of instability is present for these storms 
given the hot and humid conditions that remain across the region
(2000-3000 J/kg of MUCAPE), so thinking some updrafts could be 
on the perkier side. Very little in the way of wind shear is 
present across the region though (0-6km bulk shear of 20kts or 
less), so storms will struggle to sustain themselves leading to 
low potential for severe hazards. However, some small hail and 
gusty winds are possible under the stronger updrafts. 

Overnight, anticipating areas of fog to develop as low level 
ridging begins to build into the region. The soupy conditions 
and diminishing winds within the stabilizing atmosphere should 
result in conditions primed for fog development. Would expect 
fog to be dense at times with the 04.12z HREF suggesting 20-40% 
probabilities for visibilities less than 1/4mi. Fog will 
dissipate through around 9-10am Saturday morning. 

Heading into the holiday weekend, upper level ridging builds 
across the central United States allowing for northwest upper 
level flow to set up across the Upper Mississippi River Valley. 
A couple shortwave impulses are progged to move through the 
region within the mean flow, sparking periods of showers and 
storms (30-50%), most favorable Saturday night into Sunday and 
west of the Mississippi River. Strong to severe storms appear 
unlikely though as upper level winds, and by association the 
wind shear, should be rather light. Shower/storm coverage may 
also end up being rather scattered given low level dry air in 
place, resulting in a cap across the region.

High pressure sinking southward across the Great Lakes through 
the weekend should also force the boundary that's been over the 
region through the better part of the week to southward, 
allowing for a slight and brief cooling trend Sunday into 
Monday. Temperatures will still be above normal, though only by 
5-10 degrees rather than the 10-15 degrees we've seen this past 
week. Currently expecting highs to top out in the upper 70s to 
low 80s with the 25th-75th percentiles of ensemble guidance 
highlighting this as the most favorable range. This trend will 
be short-lived though as temperatures begin to warm again 
through mid-week.

Tuesday - Wednesday: Low Pressure System and Shower/Storm Chances

Greater potential for showers and storms area-wide comes 
Tuesday into Wednesday when the longwave trough currently 
situated over the Pacific Northwest ejects eastward and deepens 
a surface low across the northern Great Plains. An associated 
cold front is expected to move through the Upper Midwest as the 
low shifts eastward across southern Canada which will be the 
main focus for these shower and storm chances. 

Many of the members of the various ensemble suites 
(GEFS/ENS/GEPS) do highlight precipitation moving through the 
region with this cold front, though there is some variation 
regarding timing and location. Currently, rainfall probabilities
in the 04.13z NBM sit around 50-70% across our area, though are
highest north of our area where 1000-500hPa QG convergence is 
maximized. There is also the potential influence of dry low 
level air across much of the Upper Mississippi River Valley as 
suggested by the 04.12z GFS solution which would limit 
shower/storm development along the cold front and could result 
in lower probabilities. Regardless, some storms that develop 
could be on the stronger side given 35-40kts of 0-6km bulk
shear, MLCAPE on the order of 750-1250 J/kg, and AI/ML guidance
highlighting some low potential for strong storms.
